target_customer: Enterprises and Fortune 500 security teams managing end of life and outdated open source software
problem: End of life software holds unpatched vulnerabilities with few remediation paths. Xeol finds it in container images, filesystems and SBOMs so firms can manage it proactively.
business_model: Open source scanner (Apache licensed) plus an enterprise platform and EOL dataset
product_category: Software supply chain security, end of life detection

founders.name: ShiHan Wan
founders.background_notes: Backend engineer who helped build two startups from early stage to unicorn valuations per YC. Was Director of Platform Engineering at Electric per press.

technical_complexity.rationale: Scanning images and SBOMs is standard tooling, but maintaining an accurate dataset of end of life status for over 100,000 packages is continuous work.

defensibility.rationale: The scanner was open source and free, so the dataset was the only asset. Data freshness lagged paid competitors per third party comparisons.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: HeroDevs, an end of life remediation vendor, bought Xeol in February 2025 and ran it as a division.

market_need_then: End of life and outdated open source dependencies were a recognised supply chain risk, and the company tied it to vulnerability management and cyber insurance cost. No quantified demand data found.

identity.logo: Wordmark, later shown beside HeroDevs as XEOL by HeroDevs

branding.brand_signature: The pronunciation note Zee-O-L, since the name reads like end of life
branding.community_and_virality: Open source scanner repository on GitHub, no merch or press on the brand found.

brand_strength.rationale: Unusual spelling needed a pronunciation guide in its YC profile. Some developer reach through open source but no brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Xeol was a small New York team building end of life dependency detection, raised a 3.2 million dollar seed in December 2023 led by Shield Capital, and was bought by HeroDevs in February 2025 with terms undisclosed. The free open source scanner and its package dataset gave a natural fit with a remediation vendor, but the thin moat and short runway suggest a tuck in rather than a breakout.
notes: CB Insights lists 3.7M total over three rounds, unverified so only the 3.2M seed is recorded. Competitor sources found were 2026 comparison sites, not dated near the batch, so the list is empty. Name origin not found.
